purpose: Remove the global enrollment identifier that defeated RC32, test every two-role view for deterministic raw-to-outcome joins, and permit an independent auditor to open exactly one preregistered disputed record.

messageGraph.custodyToPseudonymizerHandle: Fresh 128-bit synthetic routing handle unique to one enrollment event.
messageGraph.pseudonymizerToOutcomeHandle: Independent fresh 128-bit synthetic routing handle unique to the same event but unequal to every custody handle.
messageGraph.recordOrder: Each role view is independently shuffled; array position is not a permitted join key.
messageGraph.publicLedger: Contains study-local commitments and duplicate pointers but neither routing handle nor raw or outcome truth. Stable duplicate commitments do not enter the outcome view; its binding is event-specific.
messageGraph.normalOperationRule: No normal two-role union may contain a deterministic path from syntheticRawPackageId to outcomeClass.
messageGraph.threeRoleBoundary: All three operational roles together can reconstruct every raw-to-outcome path; RC33 does not claim three-role collusion resistance.

disputeCapability.format: base64url(canonical payload) || '.' || HMAC-SHA-256(auditor synthetic signing key, payload)
disputeCapability.authorization: A valid capability authorizes the resolver to return the one registry bridge bound to its auditRecordId.
disputeCapability.replayState: The resolver stores the capability digest after redemption and rejects reuse.
disputeCapability.oneTimeBoundary: One-time use is a stateful resolver guarantee, not a property that prevents a copied bearer token from being presented first.
reject: bridge opening more than one record

hypotheses.claim: Replacing a global enrollment ID with two independent hop handles reduces deterministic raw-to-outcome joins to zero in every two-role operational view.
hypotheses.rejectWhen: Any custody-pseudonymizer, custody-outcome, or pseudonymizer-outcome union yields at least one deterministic raw-to-outcome path.

hypotheses.claim: A scoped auditor capability opens exactly one disputed bridge and rejects replay, tampering, wrong-dispute, expiry, and cross-record use.
hypotheses.rejectWhen: The valid capability opens zero or multiple bridges, or any negative control opens a bridge.

hypotheses.claim: Pairwise handle separation and a VOPRF are interchangeable privacy claims.
hypotheses.rejectWhen: VOPRF proof conformance leaves a stable transport join, or unlinkable transport handles provide no cryptographic input blindness.

safety: All packages, identifiers, keys, vendors, outcomes, disputes, and observations are synthetic. The protocol contains no production secret, customer record, real hardware identifier, or live authorization.
